newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN says refugees dying in Zaire jungles, rivers.
newsitem.headline: UN says refugees dying in Zaire jungles, rivers.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Friday that Rwandan Hutu refugees were dying in Zaire's jungles and drowning while crossing rivers and expressed alarm at their plight as the rainy season begins.

Spokesman Kris Janowski said the rainy season would further complicate aid efforts in the remote rainforests of east Zaire, turn grass landing strips into mud and leave aid agencies with only one option to transport supplies across rivers -- by boat.

Up to 100,000 hungry and exhausted refugees have arrived at the town of Ubundu on the Zaire River upstream from the eastern town of Kisangani after a long trek across the rainforest, fleeing advances by mainly Tutsi rebels fighting Zairean troops.
World Food Programme spokeswoman Christiane Berthiaume said a U.N. aid flight carrying food for refugees in Ubundu had to be cancelled on Friday because rains made landing impossible.
The refugees have been plunging deeper into Zaire with each rumoured rebel attack and aid agencies have been following them with difficulty.
Beyond Ubundu, Janowski said, "it is total wilderness. We'd have no logistics to help the refugees."
Janowski said some refugees were so weak they could not carry their small children and left them behind in the jungle.
"It was a harrowing journey. The refugees have had enough. They are in a terrible shape. There's been a trail of bodies left behind the refugees in the jungle," he told a briefing.
The refugees are hostage to Hutu militia and ex-soldiers who led 1994's genocide of minority Tutsis and cannot go back peacefully to Rwanda where a Tutsi-dominated army holds sway.
Many refugees killed or watched others kill during the slaughter of more than half a million Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
The UNHCR failed to separate militia from the refugees at vast refugee camps in eastern Zaire and the world refused to send in troops to do the job, setting the stage for today's conflict.
The rebels say they are advancing towards eastern Zaire's military and regional hub Kisangani, defended by Zairean troops, foreign mercenaries and allied Rwandan Hutu militiamen.
Janowski said Hutu militiamen were accompanying the refugees but that UNHCR had no evidence they were forcing them deeper into Zaire on a death march.
He could not give a number for refugees who died in the jungle or when crossing the river on the way to Ubundu.
Some 200,000 Rwandan Hutus remain unaccounted for after they fled an earlier rebel advance on Tingi-Tingi camps, the UNHCR says.
The rebels say they want to topple Zaire's ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko, who is in France after surgery for prostate cancer in Switzerland last August.
